newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Arafat start talks at White House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Arafat start talks at White House.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday opened talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat by saying he regretted Israel's decision to build new housing for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, saying it bred "mistrust."

"I would have preferred the decision not have been made because I don't think it builds confidence, I think it builds mistrust," Clinton told reporters at the start of his White House meeting with Arafat.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government decided last week to build 6,500 homes for Jews on Jabal Abu Ghneim, a pine-covered hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem known by Israelis as Har Homa.
Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and views the entire city as its capital but the Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state.
Arafat said on Monday he believed the Israelis wanted to isolate Jerusalem. "Their target is to squeeze and to isolate Jerusalem," Arafat told reporters at the start of the meeting.

Noting that Arafat's last White House visit took place in early October, when the United States sought to revive talks on Israel's much-delayed troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron, Clinton said: "This is also a difficult moment but I think we can work through it and go forward."
